# Methods
## Exploratory Analysis
```{r}
#| label: summary statistics & examining the distribution of the dependent variable and 

#regdata <- read.csv("~/GitHub/MUSA-5000-portfolio/HW1/RegressionData.csv")
regdata <- read.csv("RegressionData.csv")
#names(regdata) # gets the names of each variable.

regdata <- regdata %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), as.numeric)) # some of them were returning a string, we need a number to run summary statistics.

vars <- c("MEDHVAL","PCTBACHMOR", "NBELPOV100", "PCTVACANT", "PCTSINGLES")

sum_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("Median House Value",
                        "# Households Living in Poverty",
                        "% with Bachelor's Degree or Higher",
                        "% Vacant Houses",
                        "% Single House Units"),
  Mean = sapply(regdata[vars], mean, na.rm = TRUE), #creates column of mean values for each variable, ignoring null values.
  SD = sapply(regdata[vars], sd, na.rm = TRUE) #creates column of sd values for each variable, ignoring null values.
)

sum_table

#running hist on all of the variables we defined above
for (v in vars){
  hist(regdata[[v]],
       main = paste("Distribution of ", v),
       xlab =v,
       col = "lightblue",
       border = "darkblue")
}

```
```{r}
#| label: log transformations and its effect on the distribution

regdata <- regdata %>%
  mutate(LNMEDHVAL    = log(MEDHVAL),
         LNPCTBACHMOR = log(1 + PCTBACHMOR),
         LNBELPOV100 = log(1 + NBELPOV100),
         LNPCTVACANT  = log(1 + PCTVACANT),
         LNPCTSINGLES = log(1 + PCTSINGLES))

hist(regdata$MEDHVAL,     main = "MEDHVAL",     xlab = "MEDHVAL",col = "lightblue",border = "darkblue")
hist(regdata$LNMEDHVAL,   main = "LNMEDHVAL",   xlab = "LNMEDHVAL",col = "lightblue",border = "darkblue")


hist(regdata$PCTBACHMOR,  main = "PCTBACHMOR",  xlab = "PCTBACHMOR",col = "lightblue",border = "darkblue")

hist(regdata$PCTVACANT,  main = "PCTVACANT",  xlab = "PCTVACANT",col = "lightblue",border = "darkblue")

hist(regdata$PCTSINGLES,  main = "PCTSINGLES",  xlab = "PCTSINGLES",col = "lightblue",border = "darkblue")
```

## b.
```{r}
#| label: Scatter plot for each predictor
#| message: false
#| warning: false

regdata %>%
  dplyr::select(LNMEDHVAL, PCTBACHMOR, LNBELPOV100, PCTVACANT, PCTSINGLES) %>%
  pivot_longer(-LNMEDHVAL, names_to = "Predictor", values_to = "Value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Value, y = LNMEDHVAL)) +

  labs(x = NULL, y = "LNMEDHVAL")

```

## d.
```{r}
#| label: Chloropleth maps of each variable using the sf (simple features) and ggplot packages
#| note: readOGR has been officially retired as a part of the rgdal library.

#shapefile <- "~/GitHub/hw-1-musa5000/Lecture 1 - RegressionData.shp/RegressionData.shp"
shapefile <- "Lecture 1 - RegressionData.shp/RegressionData.shp"

c_map = read_sf(shapefile)

#names(c_map)

c_map <- c_map %>%
  mutate(LNMEDHVAL    = log(MEDHVAL),
         LNBELPOV100 = log(1 + NBelPov100),
         PCTVACANT, PCTSINGLES, PCTBACHMOR)

#maps the log of the dependent variable: LNMEDHVAL
ggplot(c_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill=LNMEDHVAL))+
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1)+
  theme_void()+
  labs(title = "Log of Median House Value")

# maps 2-5: the four predictors
p1 <- ggplot(c_map) + geom_sf(aes(fill = LNBELPOV100)) +scale_fill_distiller(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1) + theme_void() + labs(title = "LNBELPOV100")
p2 <- ggplot(c_map) + geom_sf(aes(fill = PCTBACHMOR))   +scale_fill_distiller(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1) + theme_void() + labs(title = "PCTBACHMOR")
p3 <- ggplot(c_map) + geom_sf(aes(fill = PCTVACANT))    +scale_fill_distiller(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1) + theme_void() + labs(title = "PCTVACANT")
p4 <- ggplot(c_map) + geom_sf(aes(fill = PCTSINGLES))   +scale_fill_distiller(palette = "BuPu", direction = 1) + theme_void() +labs(title = "PCTSINGLES")

# combine into one 2x2 figure
(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)
```

## Stepwise Regression
# Sophia
```{r}
#| label: Using Stepwise regression to determine the best model based on the Akaike Information Criterion

# Full OLS model with all four predictors
model_full <- lm(
  LNMEDHVAL ~ PCTVACANT + PCTSINGLES + PCTBACHMOR + LNBELPOV100,
  data = regdata
)

summary(model_full)
```
```{r}
# Stepwise regression using AIC
step_model <- step(model_full)

step_model
```
```{r}
# View the sequence of models considered
step_model$anova
```
```{r}
# Show the final model selected by stepwise regression
formula(step_model)
```

## K-fold Cross Validation
# Sophia
```{r}
#| label: calculating RMSE and re-running the model with two predictors: PCTVACANT and MEDHHINC 

# 5-fold cross-validation for the full four-predictor model
cv_full <- CVlm(
  data = regdata,
  form.lm = model_full,
  m = 5,
  plotit = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
names(cv_full)
str(cv_full)
```

```{r}
# Calculate RMSE for the full model
rmse_full <- sqrt(
  mean((cv_full$LNMEDHVAL - cv_full$cvpred)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
)
rmse_full
```
```{r}
# Model with PCTVACANT and MEDHHINC
model_two <- lm(
  LNMEDHVAL ~ PCTVACANT + MEDHHINC,
  data = regdata
)
summary(model_two)

# 5-fold cross-validation
cv_two <- CVlm(
  data = regdata,
  form.lm = model_two,
  m = 5,
  plotit = FALSE
)

# Calculate 5-fold cross-validation RMSE
rmse_two <- sqrt(
  mean((cv_two$LNMEDHVAL - cv_two$cvpred)^2, na.rm = TRUE)
)

rmse_two
```
```{r}
rmse_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Full model: 4 predictors",
    "Reduced model: PCTVACANT + MEDHHINC"
  ),
  RMSE = c(rmse_full, rmse_two)
)

rmse_results
```
